prompt:
Write an original mystery story titled "The Tide Register".

Write this story in English.
Use third-person narration outside quoted speech and dreams.
Use past-tense narration outside quoted speech and dreams.
Preserve this physical rule: The tide bell is operated by a manual lever; it cannot ring without someone moving the lever.
Follow the supplied three-chapter order.
Keep the tide register intact until its custody transfer in chapter three.
Keep Ivo alive through the end of chapter three.
Present remembered scenes as past events rather than current events.

Use the supplied character, place and chronology bible. Let the unresolved questions develop through the supplied outline without treating a plan or dream as an event.

outline.title: The Duplicate Tide
outline.purpose: Develop The Tide Register through its planned state changes.
outline.turn: The pay register named Ivo Marr as a dock clerk.
hookSeeds: The register contained two entries for the same tide.
A blue thread protruded from the register’s stitched spine.
Rook wore a square impression of clean skin where his ring should have been.

outline.title: The Lever in the Rain
outline.purpose: Develop The Tide Register through its planned state changes.
outline.turn: Lena found Rook beneath the broken rail; he was dead.
hookSeeds: The second tide entry matched the hour on the watch log.
The blue thread remained visible along the wet spine.
A crescent of green wax clung to the bridge lever.

outline.title: The Open Register
outline.purpose: Develop The Tide Register through its planned state changes.
outline.turn: The hearing clerk entered Ivo in the record as a municipal witness.
hookSeeds: The duplicate entry concealed a second docking fee.
The blue thread marked the pocket holding the fee receipt.
Rook had pledged his ring to cover the missing fee.
The green wax came from the council’s receipt seal.

authorIntent: Let changing evidence alter trust without turning uncertainty into a completed event.
currentFocus: Preserve the difference between confirmed state, speech, recollection and conjecture.
